670. The brethren said, ' ' Why is it that, although all the 1 fathers used to admonish the brethren to ask the old men 1 questions continually, and to learn from them, and to reveal ' to them their thoughts, and to live according to their direc- 1 tions, one of the old men said to one of the brethren, 'Go, ' 'sit in thy cell, and thy cell shall teach thee everything'?"

The old man said, "There is no contradiction in these words ' of the Fathers, and what the old man said hath an object, ' the meaning of which is well known. The old man who ad- ' monished the brother that he should learn like a beginner ' was great and famous, and to that brother who asked him 'the question he spake thus: — In the early days when thou ' goest to thy cell lay hold upon the habits (or orders) of the ' neophytes, and live according to them for a considerable ' period, that is to say, with fasting, and vigil, and reading, ' and reciting the offices, and all the other things, until at ' length, after the lapse of time, the life of contemplation in ' silence shall give thee the order which befitteth thy seclusion, ' and will add those things which are seemly, and will diminish ' those which are not. This is the meaning of that which was ' said by the holy man, 'Sit in thy cell, and it shall teach thee ' ' everything.'"

671. The brethren said, "One of the old men used to say, ' ' A man shall have no care, and he shall contemplate in ' ' silence, and shall cover up himself; three meditations shall ' ' teach purity.' What is the meaning of these three words?"

The old man said, " ' A man shall have no care' means that ' he shall not care concerning the shortcomings of others, and ' that all his anxiety shall be concerning his own shortcomings. ' And, 'He shall contemplate in silence' means that he shall ' not speak even concerning matters of spiritual excellence 'if it will trouble any man or condemn him. And 'He shall ''cover up himself meaneth that he shall not reveal his ' life and deeds, but as far as possible, he shall be un- ' known and unhonoured. Now by these things is esta-

672. The brethren said, "How is it possible for a monk to die every day for the love of Christ, even as the blessed Paul said, 'I swear by your boasting, my brethren, that, in our i Lord Jesus Christ, I die daily, and the world is dead unto 1 me, and I am crucified unto the world, and the world is ' crucified unto me, and I live, yet not I, but Christ liveth in i me'?" The old man said, "A man [can do this] if he con- template in silence at all seasons, and perform the other works of the body, I mean fasting, and vigil, and the recital of the books of the Psalms, and prayers, and genuflexions, and groanings, and pain, and weeping, and tears, and sighs, and the reading of the Holy Scriptures. And he must espe- cially take care concerning the works of the mind, that is, the constant remembrance of God, and meditation upon Him and His blessings, and upon His commandments and His threatenings; and his gaze must always be on our Lord, and his prayer must be without ceasing and without wandering, and the odiousness of the passions must be away from the heart, and he must suppress with keenness the thoughts of the devils which arise at their prompting. And he must possess that excellence which is the first and most important of all the spiritual virtues, and of all the labours of the ascetic life of the mind, that is to say, death in respect of all the anxieties and cares of this world. And a monk must have no care, and no anxiety, and he must not think about anything, or seek anything, or desire anything, or lust for anything, except for the time when he will attain to the perfect love of God in our Lord Jesus Christ. And he must fulfil at all times the command of the blessed Paul, and his admonition to us wherein he said, 'Love ye your Lord, rejoice in your hope, 1 pray without ceasing, be fervent in spirit, endure your 1 tribulations, be not anxious about anything, cast all your 1 care upon the Lord; and let all your prayers, and all your * requests, and all your petitions be made known unto God, ' to Whom be glory for ever and ever! Amen.'"

673. The brethren said, M How can love be acquired by men of understanding?" The old man said, "True and pure love is the way of life, and the haven of promises, and the trea- sure of faith, and it sheweth [the way of] the kingdom, and it is the expositor of the judgement, and the preacher concern- ing what is hidden."
674. The brethren said, " We do not know the power of the word." The old man said, " If a man doth not love God he will not believe in Him, and His promises are not certain to

And he doth 41 this because His judgement is raised too far above his eyes. 44 Therefore let us run after love, wherein the holy fathers 44 were rich, for it is able to reward its nature and its God, and " this is its praise."

675* The brethren said, 4< In what way doth wisdom live in 44 a man?" The old man said, 44 Now when a man hath gone " forth to follow God with a sincere mind, grace taketh up its 44 abode in him, and his life and deeds are strengthened in the 44 Spirit, and he hath taken a hatred to the world, for he per- 44 ceiveth that new spiritual life which is in the new man, and 44 which is exalted above the impurity of human life, and in 44 his mind he thinketh upon the humility of the life and works 44 which are to come, and which are [more] excellent than those 44 here."
676. The brethren said, 4< By what is love made known?" The old man said, 44 By the fulfilment of work, and by spiri- 44 tual meditation and by the knowledge of faith."

677* The brethren said, 44 What are works?" The old man said, 44 The keeping of the commandments of God in the purity 44 of the inner man, together with the [performance of] labours 44 by the outer man."

678. The brethren said, 44 Is every man who is destitute of 44 works also destitute of love?" The old man said, 44 It is im- 44 possible for the man who is in God not to love and it is 44 impossible that he who loveth should not work; and it is incre- 44dible that he who teacheth and doth not work is indeed a 44 believer, for his tongue is the enemy of his actions, and al- though he speaketh life, he is in subjection unto death."

679. The brethren said, 44 And is he who is in this state de- 44stitute of reward?" The old man said, 44The man who 44 speaketh the things of the spirit, and who performeth the 44 things of the body is not destitute of reward, and that which 44 he needeth is fulfilled for him, but he is deprived of the crown 44 of light, because he desireth not that the rule of the spirit 44 shall have dominion over him."

680. The brethren said, 44 Fasting and prayer: what are 44 they?" The old man said, 44Fasting is the subjugation of 44 the body, and prayer is converse with God, vigil is the war 44 with Satan, abstinence is the being weaned from meats, 44 standing up is the humility of the primitive man, genuflexion 44 is the bowing down before the Judge, tears are the remem- 44brance of sins, nakedness is our captivity through trans-

681. The brethren said, "Are these things able to redeem 1 the soul?" The old man said, "When the things which are 4 within agree with the things which are without and the hu- 4 mility which is manifest appeareth in the hidden works 4 which are within, in very truth a man is redeemed from the 4 heaviness of the body."
682. The brethren said, 44And what is internal humility?" The old man said, 44 It is humility of love, peace, concord,

4 purity, restfulness, gentleness, subjection, faith, remoteness 4 from envy, [and it is] the soul which lacketh the fervour of 1 anger, and is remote from the lust of arrogance, and is 4 separated from vainglory, and is filled with patient endur- 4 ance like the great deep, and whose motion is drawn after 4 the knowledge of the spirit, and before whose eyes is de- 4 picked the departure from the body, and the great marvel of 4 the Resurrection, and the call tojudgement, which [shall come] 4 after the quickening, and its standing before the awful throne 4 of God, and the being redeemed."
683. The brethren said, 44 Is it possible for a man to fast and 4 not to be redeemed?" The old man said, 44 There is a fasting 4 which is a matter of habit, and another which is of desire,

4 and another which is of constraint, and another which is of 4 the sight, and another which is of vainglory, and another of 4 tribulation, andanother of repentance, and another of spiritual 4 love; and although each one of them is the same outside the 4 mind, yet in the word of knowledge they are distinct. Now 4 although the manner of each in respect of the body is the 4 same, yet each should be undertaken with thorough pur- 4 pose, and a man should journey straightly along the way of 4 love, and should bear his burden with spiritual patience, and 4 he should not rejoice in his honour."
684. The brethren said, 44Who is the true [monk]?" The old man said, 4<He who maketh his word manifest indeed, and en-
4 dureth his pain patiently; with such a man new life is found, 4 and the knowledge of the spirit dwelleth in him."
685. The brethren said, 44Who is he that liveth purely?" The old man said, 44 He who is free from the delights of the body,
4 and who rejoiceth in the love of his neighbours in the love of 4 God; for in proportion as need hath rule over the soul is 4 spiritual repose produced [therein]."
686. The brethren said, 44With what can we vanquish lust?" The old man said, 44With the remembrance of the good things
4 of the spirit; for, if the desire for the good things which are 4 to come doth not abrogate the lust for the delights of this

687. The brethren said, "In what way doth a man go forth from the world?" The old man said, "He doeth this when he forsaketh the gratification of all his lust, and when, so far as it lieth in his power, he runneth to fulfil the commandments; the man who doth not do this will fall."

688. The brethren said, "Through what did the men of old triumph over nature?" The old man said, "Through the fervour of their love which was above nature, and through the death of the man which is corruptible, and through con- tempt of arrogance, and through abatement of the belly, and through the fear of the judgement, and through the sure and certain promise; through the desire of these glorious things the Fathers acquired in the soul a spiritual body."
689. The brethren said, "How can we vanquish the passions which afflicl; us, since they are placed in our nature?" The old

man said, "Through your death to the world, for except a man burieth himself in the grave of continence the spiritual Adam can never be quickened in him. For when a dead man de- parteth from this temporary life, he hath no perception of the world, and all his senses are at rest and they are useless. Now if that which appertaineth to thy natural body thou dost for- sake naturally, and thou dost not do the same voluntarily in respect of thine own person, thou wilt die; but if thy desire dieth through repentance, [thy] nature will cease from this temporary life in the death of the spirit, even as the natural emotions of the body ceased through its natural end."
